detail: Pack-evolution closure audit round 1, correctness-and-non-regression lens. NOT READY: 1 blocker, 8 major, 8 minor. The blocker was the one the coordinator could not have found by re-reading its own work - a headline figure that did not reproduce from the grid the release ships. Killed 14 of 17 injected mutants and reported the 3 survivors as findings, each a genuinely unpinned branch. One finding was true at the audited revision and already false at HEAD, an artifact of auditing a moving branch - the dispatcher's defect, not the auditor's. Disclosed unprompted that it had dirtied the snapshot index once and restored it. ~45 min, 219k tokens, 129 tool calls.

Round 1, architecture-and-honesty lens, concurrent with and blind to the correctness lens. NOT READY: 4 blockers, 8 major, 9 minor. THE TWO POPULATIONS WERE ALMOST DISJOINT - 3 findings of 29 overlapped - the second measurement of that property and the strongest argument for the two-auditor tier. Its unique blockers were all in the layer the release is named for: a derived-view file contradicted by the command printed twelve lines below it, a budget breach disclosed at the previous release and deleted at this one, instructional surfaces telling a project to build the pin the release calls unverifiable, and a template declaring the candidate itself adoptable. Killed 23 of 23 injected mutants. Detected and corrected its own false-kill harness defect mid-audit and re-ran every affected mutant. ~47 min, 243k tokens, 127 tool calls.

Round 2, did-the-repairs-actually-repair lens. NOT READY: 4 blockers, 3 major, 6 minor. Reverted all 21 code repairs and the suite caught every one - then showed that the EVIDENCE repairs had not held: the divergence figure was corrected onto the grid that had just been replaced, in the same commit that widened it. Named the pattern that became this release's central lesson: repairs were strong wherever a test was written against behaviour and weak wherever a number in prose stood in for a measurement. ~30 min, 163k tokens, 101 tool calls.

Round 2, non-regression-and-honesty lens, concurrent and blind. NOT READY: 7 blockers, 8 major, 9 minor, again almost disjoint from its partner. Found the only genuine REGRESSION of the session: a repair had let a trailer through that the qualified baseline refused. Also ran 143,820 single-pattern comparisons and 1,500 generated negation sets against real git check-ignore with zero divergences, and enumerated every pair where an exemption widened, showing each was a case where the baseline disagreed with git and the candidate agrees. ~30 min, 223k tokens, 95 tool calls.

Round 3, adversarial lens. NOT READY: 3 blockers, 4 major, 3 minor. Removed the -z from all ten path enumerations to prove one binding test genuinely universal, then found four more classes the commit gate accepted that the baseline refused - an invisible character, a doubled bang, an empty scope, two scope groups - by exhaustive and randomised differential over 152,652 subjects. Also identified the coordinator's own differential grid as a hand-written list on exactly the axes that broke. ~23 min, 186k tokens, 63 tool calls.

Round 3, release-readiness lens, concurrent and blind. NOT READY: 3 blockers, 5 major, 7 minor. Read the release packet as the release authority would and found it written before the previous round and never revisited - it disclosed neither that any audit had returned NOT READY nor that a repair had regressed the gate. Also found the recorded adapter digests truncated below what the pack's own verifier accepts, and a decision contradicted by two shipped drill documents. Ran 111,267 pattern comparisons against git with zero divergences. ~25 min, 201k tokens, 98 tool calls.

NOT a capability finding. The reviewer adapter's isolation mode had been removed and the corrected file was on disk; auditors dispatched afterwards in the same session were still given worktrees, and refs/heads/worktree-agent-* refs appeared inside the audited repository - where publication_gate.py refused them by name, having reported the same namespace clean an hour earlier. The harness loads an adapter definition at session start, so editing it later changes the file and not the behaviour. Recorded because it is the reason adapter verification belongs at capability open, before the first dispatch.
provenance: RP2.2 evolution session; found by dispatching the closure auditors

detail: Round 4, break-it lens. NOT READY: 3 blockers, 3 major. Found the round-3 repairs had no oracle - reverted four of them and the whole suite stayed green, then committed the mutation and refreshed the digest so the release's own verification command passed too. Also found a Unicode space after a bullet marker hid a trailer, an exponential blowup in ** matching this release introduced, and three pathmatch gaps by differential. ~28 min, 214k tokens, 119 tool calls.

Round 4, release-authority lens, concurrent and blind. NOT READY: 2 blockers, 1 major, 8 minor. Found the refuted divergence figure still shipping in the prose of the test module that computes the real one, surviving because the guard exempted that file by name - the hand-written-list shape the same commit says it rejects - and found the packet claiming every injected mutation was killed every time, which the release's own round-1 record contradicts. Independently reproduced the contaminated-oracle failure, generating thousands of fictional divergences before isolating it. ~26 min, 198k tokens, 104 tool calls.

NOT an audit round; the audit budget was already spent. Ran the shipped tools read-only against the three real PROJECT.yaml files on this machine, which no round had ever done. Two defects: the contract reader raised on a live project's contract and made it unreadable by every tool over one optional block, because this release invented a field spelling the real project does not use and treated an absent identity field as an error; and the pin classifier answered about a project whose contract it had never opened, reporting a well-formed four-field pin as legacy. A third followed from the same probe: every CLI exited on an unhandled traceback when git could not answer, so a refusal was indistinguishable from a bug in the tool. All three repaired, seven mutations killed. ~35 min.
evidence: docs/RP2.2-GATE.md, After the audit budget closed

detail: Round 5, real-consumer compatibility lens, mandate explicitly not a repository review. NOT READY: 3 blockers, 8 recommended. Highest value: two readiness components answered by restating the project's own claim rather than reading the release, and a release index was consumed as trusted input by the module that composes the one calling it untrusted - it announced an unqualified release and a nonexistent root as available qualified releases. Also took line coverage over the whole suite and found a path no test executes that a real contract does, then reverted it and showed a project pointed at the wrong release reporting READY with the suite green. Independently re-killed the seven earlier mutations and confirmed the gate's claim about them was true. Distinguished two equivalent mutants from real findings and said so. ~43 min, 194k tokens, 75 tool calls.

Round 5, release non-regression and unsupported-claims lens, concurrent and blind. NOT READY: 3 blockers, 4 recommended. Found the same script-versus-module crash the coordinator was repairing concurrently, and independently found that the structural test guarding the refusal wrapper was vacuous - it grepped for a string, and only 5 of 17 CLIs were executed anywhere in the suite. Also found the manifest quoting the baseline's line count with this release's own percentage, concealing that held prose grew from 14.9 to 24.3 percent over target. Verified the public-safety claim in both halves by execution. Noticed the audited working tree going dirty mid-run, attributed it correctly to a concurrent process, and drew no conclusion from it. ~40 min, 165k tokens, 98 tool calls.

Round 6, convergence lens against the repaired candidate. READY, no blockers, 2 recommended. Reproduced nine of ten prior defects as closed by execution and ran fourteen targeted mutations, all killed, plus fifteen constructed false-READY attacks, all refused. Recomputed the tree digest from the algorithm description rather than by importing the module, and measured every contract-reading CLI's exit status before and after an error-hierarchy change to show it was caller-neutral. Its best finding was a residue in the class the previous round had repaired: UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, not an OSError, so a file whose bytes cannot be decoded still printed a traceback from the guard whose own comment denies it - falsified in one command. Also observed that the test written to forbid tracebacks had an all-UTF-8 corpus and so could not constrain its own stated invariant. ~18 min, 130k tokens, 54 tool calls.

Round 6, release-authority lens, concurrent and blind. NOT READY: 5 blockers, 4 recommended, every one in the documents a release authority reads and none in the code - its own summary was that the code, tests and release identity survived every attempt it made. All five were the same class: a figure typed beside a fact the repository can compute. Measured 25 local-path files where the record said 21, 32 commits where it said 28, and a decision layer ending at D22 where two pointers said D19. Also warned that a mutation dying only to the two release-identity tests has not been caught by anything behavioural, having hit exactly that and had to re-run to find which of its kills were real. Zero false positives across five blockers and four recommendations. ~28 min, 131k tokens, 85 tool calls.

NOT A PROPERTY OF THE ROUTE OR THE MODEL — the identical brief with stdin closed produced 11KB of progress in 20 seconds and a complete report in 18 minutes. Recorded because the obvious inference from these two runs, that this route is unreliable, is FALSE and would have been a durable false fact about somebody else's software. Environmental, so it charges no budget.
